name: ath10k_start
prose: static int ath10k_start(struct ieee80211_hw *hw) at mac.c:5192-5407 (mac80211 start callback; slice cut the head). Precondition: hw->priv is an ath10k device; the caller is mac80211 and may sleep. Postcondition: it calls ath10k_drain_tx (5204) and takes ar->conf_mutex (5206), which is released on every return. By ar->state: OFF becomes ON and RESTARTING becomes RESTARTED (5208-5214); ON, RESTARTED or WEDGED give a WARN_ON and -EINVAL, and UTF gives -EBUSY, both leaving the state unchanged (5215-5223). If ar->hw_rfkill_on is set under data_lock, it clears that flag and jumps to err with ret still 0, so it returns 0 without powering up and with ar->state left as ON/RESTARTED (5228-5231). Otherwise it powers up the hif and starts the core in normal mode; a failure of hif power up goes to err_off (state back to OFF) and of core start goes to err_power_down (5236-5247). It then configures rfkill (if the firmware advertises it), and sets a series of firmware parameters (PMF QoS, dynamic BW, prob-req OUI, adaptive QCS, burst off, idle_ps_config, ARP AC override, adaptive CCA, ANI, peer stats period, BT-coex off and BB timing, each depending on service bits or firmware features); the first failure of these calls goes to err_core_stop, except that -EOPNOTSUPP from ath10k_mac_rfkill_config and from the idle_ps_config parameter is ignored (5250-5254, 5298-5302), and a failure to fetch the BB timing from the device tree is ignored (5372-5373). Error exits unwind in order: err_core_stop calls ath10k_core_stop, err_power_down calls ath10k_hif_power_down, err_off sets the state to OFF, and all return the last ret (5395-5406). The return value of __ath10k_set_antenna is not checked (5304). On success it clears the started-vdev count, updates the regulatory domain, starts spectral scan and thermal throttling, sets the radar confirmation state to idle (5384-5390), and returns 0 (5393).

If skb->len is below sizeof(struct wmi_ftm_cmd) it logs a warning and returns (89-92). Otherwise it reads the current sequence number and the total segment count from the segment header and computes datalen = skb->len - sizeof(*ftm) (94-99); if current_seq is 0 it resets ar->testmode.expected_seq and data_pos to 0 (101-104). Otherwise it copies the payload to ar->testmode.eventdata at data_pos (115). If the incremented expected_seq is not equal to total_segments it stores the new data_pos and returns (118-122). On the last segment it allocates a cfg80211 testmode event skb of 2 u32 plus data_pos bytes with GFP_ATOMIC, logging and returning if that fails (127-133), adds the TLV command attribute, the WMI command id and the accumulated data, freeing the new netlink skb (nl_skb) with kfree_skb and returning on any attribute failure (135-153), and finally passes it to cfg80211_testmode_event (156). name: ath11k_dp_rx_frag_h_mpdu
prose: static int ath11k_dp_rx_frag_h_mpdu(struct ath11k *ar, struct sk_buff *msdu, u32 *ring_desc) at dp_rx.c:3666-3795 (slice cut the head). Precondition: msdu->data is a valid HAL rx descriptor, ring_desc is the msdu's ring descriptor, and the caller does not hold ab->base_lock (it is taken here, 3707). Postcondition: before any lock it returns -EINVAL for a multicast/broadcast fragment (3691), for a descriptor whose sequence-control or frame-control is not valid or whose tid is greater than IEEE80211_NUM_TIDS (3694-3697; a tid equal to IEEE80211_NUM_TIDS is not rejected by this test), and for a packet with fragment number 0 and no more-fragments bit (3704). With base_lock held, a peer that is not found or whose dp_setup_done is false gives -ENOENT (3708-3720). If the tid's fragment queue is empty or its current sequence number differs, it flushes the queue and takes the new sequence number (3724-3729); a fragment number already in the bitmap returns -EINVAL (3731-3735). Otherwise the msdu is queued (in order) in rx_tid->rx_frags and the bitmap and last fragment number updated (3737-3744); a kmemdup failure for the fragment-0 ring descriptor returns -ENOMEM with the msdu still queued (3746-3753), while for later fragments the link descriptor is returned to the idle list (3755). If the set is not yet complete the reassembly timer is armed and it returns 0 with the msdu left queued (3759-3763). If complete, it drops the lock, stops the timer, retakes the lock and re-looks up the peer; then it validates the incremental PN, defragments and reinjects into REO. On success it calls ath11k_dp_rx_frags_cleanup(rx_tid, false), which purges rx_frags (so the msdu is no longer queued), and returns 0 (3786-3787). If the peer is gone or any of those steps fails, it frees the defrag skb and flushes the queue with cleanup(rx_tid, true) at err_frags_cleanup and returns ret, which is still 0 on those paths because ret is not set there (3789-3794). base_lock is released at out_unlock (3793) on every path that took it.

name: brcmf_pcie_download_fw_nvram
prose: static int brcmf_pcie_download_fw_nvram(struct brcmf_pciedev_info *devinfo, const struct firmware *fw, void *nvram, u32 nvram_len) at pcie.c:1785-1893; the packet name brcmf_pcie_download_fw is not defined in pcie.c (the function is called at pcie.c:2295) and the slice (1797-2047) holds this function plus following ones. Postcondition: it first calls brcmf_pcie_enter_download_state and returns that error immediately if it fails, before copying anything and before release_firmware, so in that case fw (and nvram) are not released here (1798-1800). It then polls that RAM word every 50 ms for up to BRCMF_PCIE_FW_UP_TIMEOUT until it changes; if it never changes it logs and returns -ENODEV, and a changed value outside the RAM range also returns -ENODEV (1867-1889). Otherwise it returns the result of brcmf_pcie_init_share_ram_info (1892).

name: brcmf_sdio_rxglom
prose: static u8 brcmf_sdio_rxglom(struct brcmf_sdio *bus, u8 rxseq) at sdio.c:1514-1726; the slice (1524-1778) starts mid-function. Precondition: the caller must not already hold the func1 host claim, since the function claims and releases it itself around its bus accesses (1623-1626, 1634-1638, 1648-1651, 1666-1669, 1678-1682). Postcondition: it returns the number of subframes in the superframe that were parsed (num), or 0 on the failure paths below. If bus->glomd (a glom descriptor) is set, it parses the 16-bit sub-frame lengths from it (an empty or odd-length descriptor is treated as length 0, 1533-1541): a sub-frame length that is too small stops the parse (1548-1553), and a failed skb allocation stops it (1570-1575); if the loop ended without a valid packet chain (pnext NULL) it frees the partial glom queue with brcmf_sdio_free_glom and sets num to 0 (1593-1596), which does not call brcmf_sdio_rxfail. The descriptor skb is then freed in either case, bus->glomd cleared and cur_read.len zeroed (1599-1601). If the glom queue is non-empty, it receives the whole chain from the bus with brcmf_sdiod_recv_chain; on an error it calls brcmf_sdio_rxfail(bus, true, false), counts rxglomfail, frees the glom and returns 0 (1630-1639). It parses the super-frame header and each sub-frame header with brcmf_sdio_hdparse; if any parse returns an error it calls brcmf_sdio_rxfail, counts rxglomfail, frees the glom, zeroes cur_read.len and returns 0 (1676-1684). name: brcmf_sdio_bus_sleep
prose: static int brcmf_sdio_bus_sleep(struct brcmf_sdio *bus, bool sleep, bool pendok) at sdio.c:965-1018 (slice cut the head). Precondition: none is checked here; this function takes no lock itself. Postcondition: it returns err, 0 unless the KSO control (keep SDIO on) fails (1016). With save-restore enabled (bus->sr_enabled, 975): if the requested state equals bus->sleeping it jumps to end without any KSO change (977-978); otherwise, for sleep it reads CHIPCLKCSR and, if its clock-select bits are zero, writes SBSDIO_ALP_AVAIL_REQ to it (982-990), then calls brcmf_sdio_kso_control(bus, false); for wake it calls brcmf_sdio_kso_control(bus, true) (991-993). If the KSO call returns an error it logs and jumps to done, returning that error with bus->sleeping unchanged, but in the sleep case the ALP_AVAIL_REQ write may already have been made, so the clock request is not necessarily unchanged (995-998). At end (reached by the normal path and by the already-in-that-state jump): for sleep and without save-restore it calls brcmf_sdio_clkctl(bus, CLK_NONE, pendok); for wake it calls brcmf_sdio_clkctl(bus, CLK_AVAIL, pendok) and re-arms the watchdog timer with brcmf_sdio_wd_timer(bus, true) (1004-1010); then it stores bus->sleeping = sleep (1011) and returns 0. Without save-restore the KSO step is skipped entirely, so it returns 0 after the clock control and the flag update.

name: brcms_c_dpc
prose: bool brcms_c_dpc(struct brcms_c_info *wlc, bool bounded) at brcmsmac/main.c:7701-7786 (slice cut the head); the interrupt bottom half. name: wlc_lcnphy_a1
prose: static void wlc_lcnphy_a1(struct brcms_phy *pi, int cal_type, int num_levels, int step_size_lg2) at brcmsmac/phy/phy_lcn.c:3589-3782 (an LCN PHY TX IQ/LO coefficient search; the packet item was an unnamed placeholder and the function does exist under this name). Precondition: pi is an initialised LCN PHY; cal_type is 0, 2, 3 or 4 (other values leave the search limit phy_c10 unset at 0, 3670-3683); it has no pointer parameter, ptr is an internal buffer. Postcondition: it returns nothing. It allocates a 131-entry s16 scratch buffer (GFP_ATOMIC) and returns at once on failure, without touching any register (3608-3610); it allocates a 20-entry u16 save area, and on failure frees the scratch buffer and returns, again before touching any register (3612-3616). Otherwise it saves PHY registers 0x6da, 0x6db and radio register RADIO_2064_REG026, writes 0xC0 to PHY register 0x93d (this register is not restored), starts a 3750 tone, sets up the loopback, saves 0x938, 0x4d7 and 0x4d8 and modifies them (3617-3638). A num_levels of 0 becomes 4 (cal_type non-zero) or 9, and a step_size_lg2 of 0 becomes 3 or 8 (3642-3653). Starting from the current coefficient pair for cal_type (wlc_lcnphy_get_cc), it repeats num_levels times (or until the step becomes 0): it adjusts the radio gain field of REG026 by sampling until clipping is seen, evaluates the nine neighbouring coefficient pairs (clamped to a per-type limit) by setting them with wlc_lcnphy_set_cc, capturing 128 samples and computing the correlation power against a stored tone, keeps the pair with the lowest power, sets it as the new centre and halves the step (3667-3768). The last chosen pair is left set as the coefficient for cal_type. Cleanup (3770-3781) then restores the loopback state, stops the tone, writes back 0x6da, 0x6db, 0x938, 0x4d7, 0x4d8 and REG026 to their saved values and frees both internal buffers.

name: iwl_v3_rate_from_v2_v3
prose: static inline u32 iwl_v3_rate_from_v2_v3(__le32 rate, bool fw_v3) at fw/api/rs.h:899-911. It converts a firmware rate_n_flags word to the host's version-3 layout. Precondition: none. Postcondition: if fw_v3 is true it returns le32_to_cpu(rate) unchanged (903-904). Otherwise, for a version-2 word, it clears the version-2 NSS indicator bit RATE_MCS_NSS_MSK_V2 (0x10, bit 4) and ORs that bit's value (0 or 1) into RATE_MCS_NSS_MSK (0x20, bit 5) of the result (906-908). The NSS indicator is a single bit in both layouts (rs.h:663-675: version 2 has MCS in bits 3-0 and NSS==2 in bit 4; version 3 has MCS in bits 4-0 and NSS==2 in bit 5). All other bits are copied, and because the new bit is ORed in without first clearing bit 5, bit 5 of the result is the OR of the input's bit 5 and bit 4; version 2 treats bits 7-5 as reserved (rs.h:679). It has no side effects.

name: iwl_v3_rate_to_v2_v3
prose: static inline __le32 iwl_v3_rate_to_v2_v3(u32 rate, bool fw_v3) at fw/api/rs.h:913-925. It converts a host version-3 rate_n_flags word to the firmware's layout. Precondition: none. Postcondition: if fw_v3 is true it returns cpu_to_le32(rate) unchanged (917-918). Otherwise it clears the version-3 NSS indicator bit RATE_MCS_NSS_MSK (0x20, bit 5) and ORs that bit's value into RATE_MCS_NSS_MSK_V2 (0x10, bit 4) of the little-endian result (920-922). The NSS indicator is a single bit (rs.h:663-675). Because the value is ORed into bit 4 without clearing it first, bit 4 of the result is the OR of the input's bit 4 (a version-3 MCS bit) and bit 5; so for a version-3 word with MCS bit 4 set the version-2 result keeps bit 4 set whatever the NSS bit was. Bit 3 and the other bits are copied unchanged. It has no side effects.
